---
title: "2 · Lorentz model"
subtitle: "Part 1 · Historical development"
---

This chapter develops the Lorentz model step by step: first the radiation from an oscillating dipole, then the driven electron oscillator, and finally the way many such oscillators scatter, absorb, and slow light.

## Topics

### 2.1 Electric dipole radiation

[Electric dipole radiation](dipole-radiation.qmd) to study the spherical-coordinate geometry, retarded fields, far-field Poynting vector, and radiated power.

### 2.2 The Lorentz oscillator

[The Lorentz oscillator](lorentz-oscillator.qmd) to study driven motion, resonance, phase, and radiation damping.

### 2.3 Optical effects - thin sheets solution

[Optical effects - thin sheets solution](optical-dispersion.qmd) to see how driven electrons scatter light and change its speed and attenuation in matter.

### 2.4 Self-consistent Maxwell-equation solution

[Self-consistent Maxwell-equation solution](maxwell-equation-approach.qmd) for the self-consistent Maxwell-equation treatment.

### 2.5 The normal Zeeman effect

[The normal Zeeman effect](normal-zeeman-effect.qmd) connects the classical electron model to the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field.
